name: Xiufeng
tagline: Zhengyang street, the lakes and the tourist heart
description: Xiufeng is central Guilin, wrapped around Zhengyang pedestrian street and the Two Rivers and Four Lakes waterway with its illuminated Sun and Moon pagodas. Streets are compact and walkable, lined with noodle shops, hostels, banks and souvenir stalls. Almost every visitor and most short-stay foreigners base themselves inside this small area.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want everything, including cafes and transport, within a 15 minute walk.
pros: Walk to lakes, restaurants and the bus hubs
Widest choice of short-term rentals and hostels
Most English-speaking services in the city
cons: Tour groups and touts on Zhengyang all day
Restaurant and rental prices inflated by tourism
Older buildings with poor sound insulation

name: Diecai
tagline: Riverside north end below Folded Brocade Hill
description: Diecai covers the northern city under Diecai and Fubo hills, where the Li River bends past old riverside lanes and morning tai chi groups. It is residential and low-key, with local wet markets, cheap canteens and easy access to the river path. Older Guilin families dominate, so daily life stays cheap and unhurried.
bestFor: Nomads who want river walks and local prices while staying a short ride from the centre.
pros: Quiet riverside paths and hill parks for daily walks
Ten minutes by scooter or bus to the centre
cons: Housing stock is mostly older walk-up blocks
Very few cafes suitable for working

name: Qixing
tagline: University side across the river with the big park
description: Qixing sits east of the Li River around Seven Star Park, Guilin's largest, and several university campuses including Guangxi Normal. That gives it student canteens, bubble tea streets, bookshops and the cheapest decent apartments in the city. Bridges put you in the tourist centre in about ten minutes on foot or by bike.
bestFor: Budget nomads and Mandarin students who want cheap rent and a young local crowd.
pros: Cheapest reasonable apartments near the centre
Seven Star Park and riverside cycling on the doorstep
Student area means late-night cheap food
cons: Quiet and half-empty during university holidays
Park charges an entry fee for non-residents
Bridge traffic backs up at rush hour

name: Xiangshan
tagline: Elephant Trunk Hill and the southern riverbank
description: Xiangshan is the district just south of the centre, named for the famous Elephant Trunk Hill rock arch where the Taohua meets the Li River. It mixes riverside parks with ordinary mid-rise residential blocks, supermarkets and the main railway station. Practical rather than pretty, but well connected and cheaper than the core.
bestFor: Nomads who travel out often and want the train station and bus links close by.
pros: Walking distance to Guilin railway station
Riverside parks with far fewer tourists
Solid mid-range rents and full-size supermarkets
cons: Streets near the station attract touts and pickpockets
Traffic noise on the main arteries
Less charming architecture than the old centre

name: Lingui
tagline: New town suburb with modern flats and clean air
description: Lingui is the planned district southwest of the old city, built out over the past 15 years with wide boulevards, new high-rise compounds, a big park and relocated government offices. Apartments are modern with lifts, insulation and proper fibre, at prices well below the tourist centre. It is calm, green and almost entirely residential.
bestFor: Longer stays where a modern, quiet apartment with fast internet matters more than nightlife.
pros: Newest buildings and most reliable internet in Guilin
Much lower rents than the central districts
Wide pavements, parks and little traffic
cons: About 25 minutes by bus into central Guilin
Sparse restaurant and cafe scene, quiet at night
Some blocks are still half occupied
